scenarios.reasoning: AIX 7.2 is EOL (April 2025). No security patches available. The OS must be replaced — however since AIX is a proprietary Unix OS, migration to a standard Linux OS (RHEL/SLES) is the recommended path rather than an update within AIX family.

scenarios.scenario_name: Switch to standard Linux Operating System
scenarios.reasoning: AIX 7.2 is a proprietary commercial Unix OS. The application is custom-developed (COBOL). Migration to a standard Linux distribution (RHEL/SLES) would align with enterprise standards, reduce specialist costs, and provide container/cloud path. COBOL runtimes exist on Linux.
triggered_by: Operating System is a commercial or proprietary non-Linux system (AIX)

scenarios.reasoning: COBOL-2014 on AIX makes ARM migration extremely complex. IBM AIX runs on IBM POWER processors, not x86 or ARM. COBOL runtime compatibility on ARM is limited. Furthermore, the application is tightly coupled to hardware-specific AIX features.
blocked_by: Legacy Windows or proprietary Unix OS

scenarios.reasoning: No application server is recorded for this application. The COBOL application appears to run directly on AIX as a 1-Tier system without a traditional application server middleware layer.

scenarios.scenario_name: Application Migration to Cloud Infrastructure (Lift & Shift)
scenarios.reasoning: The application runs on IBM AIX — a proprietary Unix OS that is not supported by public cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP). A Lift & Shift is impossible without first migrating off AIX. An OS migration to Linux must precede cloud migration.
blocked_by: Application is tightly coupled with legacy systems

scenarios.reasoning: AIX does not support Docker/container runtime. COBOL applications require specialized container support. Containerization is blocked until the OS migration to Linux is completed.
blocked_by: Application has proprietary or unknown runtime
